entries.title: Interpretation and Definition of Domestic Violence
entries.content: Domestic violence means any act of violence, threat, or intimidation committed by a person against a spouse, former spouse, child, or dependant residing in the same household, including physical abuse, sexual abuse, emotional, verbal or psychological abuse, and economic abuse.
entries.source: Prevention of Domestic Violence Act 2006, Laws of Malawi

entries.title: Application for Protection Order
entries.content: Any victim of domestic violence, or any person acting on behalf of the victim with or without their consent in urgent cases, may apply to a Magistrate Court for a protection order prohibiting the respondent from committing acts of domestic violence, entering the victim's place of residence or workplace, or communicating with the victim.
entries.source: Prevention of Domestic Violence Act 2006, Laws of Malawi

entries.title: Occupation Order
entries.content: The court may grant an occupation order declaring that the victim is entitled to occupy the matrimonial home or domestic premises to the exclusion of the respondent, regardless of whether the premises are owned or rented by the respondent.
entries.source: Prevention of Domestic Violence Act 2006, Laws of Malawi

entries.title: Duties of Police Officers
entries.content: A police officer responding to a domestic violence incident shall assist the victim by securing medical treatment, accompanying the victim to collect personal belongings, advising on legal rights, and arresting the respondent where reasonable grounds exist to believe an offence has been committed.
entries.source: Prevention of Domestic Violence Act 2006, Laws of Malawi
